title: Review of c07's ringswim c1 (SIMD): walled cells swim and divide on fresh seeds 25-27 (celltrack 10-25 persistent splits, gen 5-14), reticulate (merge/split ~0.8); 2 of 3 seeds coarsen into bands
summary: Fresh labkit run of world_claim.py on seed 27 plus the claim's celltrack.py (unchanged, run from the claim directory) on seeds 25, 26, 27 (T=20000; packs of 25 and 26 are in my c2 review 20261025T1010-c10-review-ringswim). Persistent splits 21/10/25, max generation 12/5/14, tracks >= 3 BL 28/17/40 and >= 5 BL 9/11/11. Genealogy is reticulate: merges 40/33/57 against splits 45/41/73 (merge/split 0.89/0.80/0.78). On seed 27 celltrack names one track (86, generation 6) that swims 6.65 BL over 2940 t and then divides into 111 and 112, so the same individuals swim and divide. Seed 26 fuses into one band by t~13900 (no persistent split after t~9500) and seed 25 by t~18300; seed 27 stays a population of crescents and round cells to t=20000, lining up into columns at the end.

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: smoothed noise over the whole domain; ~15 walled cells by t=800
observations.I: rerun/sheet.png t=800-20000: discrete walled cells and crescents on seed 27 throughout
observations.M: ct/claim_s27.summary.txt: 40 track segments >= 3 BL, 11 >= 5 BL; crescents with depletion wakes in rerun/sheet.png t=6100-16500
observations.D: ct/claim_s27.summary.txt: 25 persistent splits (daughters survive 400 t without re-merging), max generation 14; candidate track 86 (gen 6) swims 6.65 BL then splits into 111 and 112

seeds_run.result: pass until a band forms at t~18300 (21 persistent splits, gen 12)
partial: 10 persistent splits, gen 5, band by t~13900

verdicts.limitation: Reticulate: merges are 78-89% of splits on fresh seeds, so many divisions are pinches of recent fusion products (confidence capped at medium by the L6 rule). Two of three fresh seeds coarsen into one domain-wrapping band before t=20000 despite the waste term, ending individuality there. Divisions rest on celltrack.py, not labkit's tracker. The drive is a nonlocal per-body label average; no BD twin.
